title: API keys
description: API key management for multi-tenant apps: CSPRNG keys with an identifiable non-secret prefix, shown once and stored only as an HMAC-SHA-256 under a server pepper, constant-time verification by lookup id, tenant and scope limits, revocation, expiry, throttled last-used writes and secret-free audit events, with injected authorization and persistence.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and Web Crypto (getRandomValues, randomUUID, subtle HMAC-SHA-256) plus the Fetch Request/Response APIs: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Server-only: the pepper and the verify path must never reach a browser bundle.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Load a pepper of at least 32 random bytes from your secret store on the trusted server and pass it as pepper; never store it with the keys.

On PostgreSQL, apply schema.sql and use createSqlApiKeyStore with your query executor; on other databases implement ApiKeyStore with a unique lookup id and conditional revoke and touchLastUsed writes.
Implement authorize(actor, 'create'|'list'|'revoke', {tenantId}) and holderScopes(actor, tenantId) from your own membership and role tables.
Pick an appPrefix (for example your product initials) so leaked keys are recognizable to secret scanners and support staff.
Call authenticateRequest(keys, request, requiredScopes) at the top of each API route and return its response when ok is false.
Optionally pass onAudit to write key.created, key.revoked, key.used and key.denied events to your audit log.
limitations: One pepper per instance: rotating the pepper invalidates every existing key; there is no built-in multi-pepper verification or key rotation workflow.
Scopes are exact strings with no wildcards or hierarchy; holderScopes is read only at creation, so later removing a scope from the creator does not shrink keys already issued (revoke them).
Constant-time comparison covers the digest compare and gives unknown lookup ids the same HMAC work; database lookup timing for known versus unknown lookup ids is not equalized.
Keys carry no checksum, so typos are detected by the lookup rather than offline, and secret scanners must match the prefix pattern.
Last-used writes and audit events are best-effort: their errors are swallowed so authentication keeps working, and last-used has the configured interval's granularity.

The in-memory store is for tests and prototypes only; the SQL store is tested on PostgreSQL semantics through PGlite, which is a single connection, not on every hosted Postgres or under multi-connection load.
No rate limiting or brute-force lockout; add request rate limits (see the rate-limit module) in front of API routes.

No management HTTP routes; mount create, list and revoke behind your own signed-in API. Production secret custody, session security and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.
decisions: key format <appPrefix>_<live|test>_<12-char lookupId>_<43-char secret>; plaintext returned once
stored as HMAC-SHA-256 of the whole key under a server pepper, not plain SHA-256 or bcrypt
Authorization: Bearer only; invalid, revoked or expired → 401 invalid_token; missing scope → 403
no HTTP management routes: only the authenticateRequest helper

verification.command: npm run build && node --test tests/api-keys.test.mjs tests/api-keys-sql.test.mjs
behaviors: keys match <appPrefix>_<live|test>_<12 base62>_<43 base62>; the secret has at least 256 bits of entropy
rejection sampling discards bytes at or above 248, so each base62 character maps from exactly 4 byte values
200 generated keys have no repeated secrets or lookup ids
the stored hash equals HMAC-SHA-256(pepper, key) computed independently; the row, list and revoke outputs never contain the key, its secret or (for outputs) the hash
a different pepper cannot verify a stored key
verify looks up by lookup id only and does exactly one HMAC for known and unknown lookup ids; wrong-secret, unknown and malformed keys all fail as invalid-key without echoing the key
a key authenticates as its one tenant and fails insufficient-scope for scopes it lacks
revoked and expired keys are rejected on the next verify; keys from a non-accepted environment are refused
viewers, other tenants and non-admins are refused create, list or revoke as configured; a member cannot mint scopes they do not hold
audit events (created, revoked, used, denied) carry ids and prefixes only; a failing audit sink does not break verify
last-used is written at most once per interval, also under three concurrent verifies on PostgreSQL
authenticateRequest maps missing and invalid keys to 401 and missing scopes to 403 with RFC 6750 WWW-Authenticate challenges and no-store
schema.sql applies, rejects a non-hex key_hash, and lookup-id collisions retry through ON CONFLICT

changes: First release: core, in-memory store, PostgreSQL schema and SQL store, Bearer authentication Fetch helper.
